vulnerability.name: X11 Open Display
vulnerability.author: Thomas Shaw
vulnerability.description: Exposes the desktop X server to the network with access control disabled, the classic "open X11" misconfiguration (CVE-1999-0526). SDDM is reconfigured through a drop-in so the X server listens on TCP (port 6000) and starts with -ac, which turns off access control. Any remote client can then connect without authentication, read the screen, inject keystrokes and type commands into the logged-in desktop session. The target autologs in to a Plasma session as a non-privileged desktop user, and a flag is left in that user's home. An attacker drives the session over the network (for example Metasploit's x11_keyboard_exec opens an xterm via KRunner and runs a command as the logged-in user).
vulnerability.hint: The host answers on an unusual TCP port with no authentication; the service lets you see and drive the desktop.
vulnerability.solution: Connect to TCP 6000 with an X11 client. With access control disabled you can screenshot the display, log keystrokes, and inject keystrokes to run commands in the logged-in session (e.g. Metasploit auxiliary/scanner/x11/open_x11 then exploit/unix/x11/x11_keyboard_exec).

CyBOK.keyword: Vulnerabilities and attacks on access control misconfigurations
